title: Rafael Campos-Gottardo
text:
About


I am a quantitative and qualitative researcher with expertise in causal inference and spatial analysis who studies support for housing and housing policies in Canada. I currently work at the Global Migration Institute at Toronto Metropolitan University, where I study housing for international students as part of Bridging Divides’ Place and Infrastructure theme. I also examine individual level support for housing as part of a project with the Laurier Institute for the Study of Public Opinion and Policy (LISPOP), which I have written about in the Waterloo Region Record.
I have previously contributed to the Canadian Election Study (CES) and worked extensively as a research assistant for the Laurier Institute for the Study of Public Opinion and Policy (LISPOP), Université du Québec à Montréal, and the Centre for the Study of Democratic Citizenship.
I received a Master’s Degree in Political Science from McGill University and a Bachelor’s degree in Political Science from Wilfrid Laurier University.

title: Projects
text:
This project maps the 2025 Montreal Election Results, and allows users to overlay neighbourhood characteristics onto the results. Election results are mapped at the polling station level and coloured by the winner of that polling station. This project was created using R for data analysis (sf, dplyr) and Leaflet for visualization.
This is an early prototype

This dashboard shows the impact of the World Cup on BIXI usage in Montreal. It was created using Bixi’s open data and R for data visualization.
This is an early prototype
Available Here
















This project maps building permits for infill housing in Edmonton, overlaid on 2021 Census demographics at the dissemination block level and the city’s zoning map. Users can switch between neighbourhood characteristics such as density, dwelling type, income, and age to see where new infill is being built. This project was created using R for data analysis (sf, dplyr, cancensus) and Leaflet for visualization.
This is an early prototype

title: BIXIing to the World Cup
text:
How did the World Cup impact Bike share usage in a Canadian city that did not host any matches?
Inspired by a project examining Bike Share activity during World Cup match days in Toronto I examine the number of Bixi trips, before, during, and after two important FIFA World Cup matches. Canada’s final game against Morocco and the the World Cup final game. Despite not hosting a World Cup game Montreal still came together for the World Cup.
This dashboard shows how many Montrealers used Bixi to get around during the World Cup, with many using the service to get to and from bars and unofficial fan zones.
I also calculate the number of trips started and ended within 1km of the 17 bars recommeded by Tourisme Montréal to watch the World Cup. For the World Cup final I also calculate the number of trips started and ended within 1km of the Just for Laugh’s fan zone at Place des Festivals.

title: BIXIing to the World Cup
text:
Data & Methods

Data
Ride data was drawn from Bixi’s open data portal.


Smoothing
Lines represent the number of rides per minute smoothed to 15 minute intervals.


Baseline Comparison
For Canada’s game against Morrocco on Saturday, July 4, 2026 the baseline is the average rides per minute for Saturday June 6, 13, 20, and 27, 2026.
For the World Cup final on Sunday, July 19, 2026 the baseline represents the average number of rides per minute for the four proceeding Sundays, June 21 and 28, and July 5 and 12, 2026.


Spatial filtering
For the recommended bars the list was drawn from Tourisme Montréal’s list of 17 recommended bars and cafes to watch the World Cup. These bars include the Pub Burgundy Lion, Station des Sports, Time Out Market Montreal, Bar L’Barouf, Bar St-Laurent Frappé, Les Enfants du Rock, Café Club Social, Café Olimpico, Bishop & Bagg, Caffè Italia, Café Marinelli, Café Gelato, Café Sportivo, Bocadillo Bistro, Café Conca d’oro, Carnitas Michoacanas Leoncito, and Bruno Sport Bar.
This data encompasses the start time of all trips started or ended at the 341 stations within 1km of the address coordinates for each bar or cafe.
For the World Cup final the Just for Laugh’s fan zone was used as the “unofficial fan zone”.
This data encompasses the start time of all trips started or ended at the 89 stations within 1km of a fixed reference point for the Place des Festivals.
Station distances were computed by projecting station coordinates and the reference point into WGS 84 (EPSG:4326) and calculating straightline distance in metres.

Data: Bixi open data.
